//ConnectionStrings: LocalDB needs Encrypt=False: it has no server certificate, so an encrypted handshake fails before SQL can be reached and every request dies as HTTP 500 with 'CanConnectAsync returned false'. This key is Development-only, which is also the only environment Program.cs:41 lets carry Encrypt=False - a Production or Staging host must supply a real string through the environment or secret store. Note that user-secrets outrank this file, so a stale 'dotnet user-secrets set ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection' left over from a hosted rehearsal silently wins here and points the local run at a server the laptop cannot reach.
//Bootstrap: DemoUsers is the one switch DemoUserSeeder reads: set it to true and startup creates one signable-in account per role, so every dashboard can be opened without an administrator typing seven accounts into the users screen by hand. It used to also require the Development environment; that second condition is gone because the reviewers' hosted site needs the same accounts, which means the setting is now the whole rule on any host, in any environment. Set it to false - or delete this block - and no such account is ever created. The accounts and their passwords are listed in README.md, so treat a host that turns this on as a demonstration, not a system holding real data.
